toolkits.name: pyinaturalist
toolkits.install: pip install pyinaturalist
toolkits.summary: Python client for iNaturalist observations, taxa, species counts, and related biodiversity records.
toolkits.notes: The harness ships direct native iNaturalist API tools for basic taxon and observation search.

toolkits.name: Pl@ntNet API
toolkits.install: Set PLANTNET_API_KEY and use the built-in PlantNetIdentify tool; upstream also provides example client code.
toolkits.summary: Plant identification API with support for local-image POST requests and organ hints such as leaf or flower.
toolkits.notes: Requires a Pl@ntNet API key.

toolkits.name: pybioclip
toolkits.install: pip install pybioclip
toolkits.summary: Python package and CLI for BioCLIP-family models that can predict taxonomic labels and generate image embeddings.
toolkits.notes: Good general-purpose biodiversity image classifier when a dedicated plant-only API is not ideal.

toolkits.name: nature-id
toolkits.install: Clone the repository and run the command-line tool with the desired model bundle.
toolkits.summary: Command-line image identifier for plants, birds, and insects using models trained on iNaturalist-derived data.
toolkits.notes: Lighter-weight than some foundation-model workflows, but less general than BioCLIP.

toolkits.name: PlantCV
toolkits.install: pip install plantcv or install from conda-forge.
toolkits.summary: Open-source computer vision toolkit for plant phenotyping with modular workflows and extensive tutorials.
toolkits.notes: One of the strongest options for plant phenotyping pipelines.

toolkits.name: LeafMachine2
toolkits.install: Clone the repository and follow the upstream virtual-environment setup instructions.
toolkits.summary: Computer-vision suite for identifying, locating, and measuring vegetative, reproductive, and archival components from digital plant datasets.
toolkits.notes: More specialized than PlantCV and particularly useful for specimen-digitization pipelines.

toolkits.name: DeepForest
toolkits.install: pip install DeepForest
toolkits.summary: Python package for ecological object detection in airborne imagery, including tree crown and bird detection models.
toolkits.notes: Best when you need a practical, ready-made aerial-detection workflow.

toolkits.name: detectree2
toolkits.install: Install PyTorch, Detectron2, then pip install detectree2.
toolkits.summary: Automatic tree crown delineation package based on Mask R-CNN for aerial RGB and multispectral imagery.
toolkits.notes: Stronger choice than pure detection when crown shapes matter.

toolkits.name: TreeCountSegHeight
toolkits.install: Use the upstream Docker image or local GPU workflow.
toolkits.summary: Deep-learning system for tree counting, crown segmentation, and height prediction at large scale.
toolkits.notes: More deployment-oriented than DeepForest or detectree2 and better suited to large-scale forestry pipelines.

toolkits.name: PyTorch-Wildlife
toolkits.install: pip install PytorchWildlife
toolkits.summary: Microsoft's collaborative AI-for-conservation framework with MegaDetector and classification models.
toolkits.notes: Best current general option for wildlife image pipelines in this stack.

toolkits.name: BirdNET-Analyzer
toolkits.install: pip install birdnet-analyzer or use the upstream installers.
toolkits.summary: Scientific audio processing toolkit for bird sound recognition and large-scale acoustic analyses.
toolkits.notes: Strongest acoustic option in this first pass.

toolkits.name: Jupyter MCP Server
toolkits.install: pip install uv && configure uvx jupyter-mcp-server@latest with JUPYTER_URL and JUPYTER_TOKEN.
toolkits.summary: Notebook-aware MCP server for code execution, notebook editing, kernel management, and rich-output analysis in Jupyter.
toolkits.notes: High-value bridge when algae-system analysis should stay inside reproducible notebooks.

toolkits.name: InfluxDB 3 MCP Server
toolkits.install: Build the upstream Node server or run the provided Docker image, then configure instance URL and token.
toolkits.summary: Time-series MCP server for querying, writing, and inspecting InfluxDB 3 measurements and schemas.
toolkits.notes: Best fit when closed algal systems are heavily instrumented and data already lives in a telemetry database.

toolkits.name: LabArchives MCP Server
toolkits.install: Create the upstream Python environment, configure LabArchives API credentials and UID, then run python -m labarchives_mcp.
toolkits.summary: Electronic lab notebook MCP server for notebook search, page reads, provenance-aware uploads, and project tracking.
toolkits.notes: Useful when algal culture runs, corrective actions, and analysis outputs should be anchored in an ELN.

toolkits.name: unit-converter-mcp
toolkits.install: pip install uv && configure uvx unit-converter-mcp.
toolkits.summary: Scientific unit-conversion MCP server covering temperature, length, area, mass, volume, time, energy, pressure, power, and density.
toolkits.notes: Small but highly practical for reconciling methods, instruments, and mixed-unit literature.

toolkits.name: PyLabRobot
toolkits.install: pip install pylabrobot and configure the hardware or simulation backend you need.
toolkits.summary: Vendor-agnostic Python SDK for liquid handling, pumps, plate readers, incubators, heater shakers, and other lab automation devices.
toolkits.notes: Strong option when closed algal workflows expand into automated dosing, sampling, or multi-device lab orchestration.

toolkits.name: Opentrons
toolkits.install: Follow the upstream Protocol API setup for OT-2 or Flex and develop Python protocols against API v2.
toolkits.summary: Official Python-based automation platform for OT-2 and Flex robots with protocol, module, and labware support.
toolkits.notes: Best when the immediate target is reliable, production-grade liquid-handling protocols on Opentrons hardware.

toolkits.name: Fiji / ImageJ
toolkits.install: Download Fiji from the upstream site or use the portable application bundle, then add needed plugins through the Fiji updater.
toolkits.summary: Batteries-included scientific image-analysis platform widely used for microscopy, fluorescence, segmentation, measurement, and plugin-driven workflows.
toolkits.notes: Most practical general-purpose image workstation for plankton, biofilm, and fluorescence images.

toolkits.name: PyImageJ
toolkits.install: pip install pyimagej
toolkits.summary: Python bridge to ImageJ2/Fiji that helps move image-processing workflows into notebooks and automated pipelines.
good_for: reusing ImageJ operations in reproducible pipelines
toolkits.notes: Useful when microscopy or fluorescence analysis should live beside Jupyter-based sensor and assay analysis.

toolkits.name: CellProfiler
toolkits.install: Use the packaged desktop release or follow the source-install guide from the upstream wiki.
toolkits.summary: Open-source bioimage-analysis platform for segmentation, measurement, feature extraction, and batch processing of microscopy images.
toolkits.notes: Strong when you need reproducible segmentation-and-measurement pipelines rather than ad hoc image inspection.

toolkits.name: napari
toolkits.install: pip install "napari[all]" or install from conda-forge with a Qt backend.
toolkits.summary: Fast Python image viewer and annotation environment for N-dimensional microscopy, overlays, labels, and plugin-based review.
toolkits.notes: Best fit when automatic classifiers still need human-in-the-loop validation.

toolkits.name: ilastik
toolkits.install: Use the upstream installers or conda-based development setup from the project documentation.
toolkits.summary: Interactive machine-learning toolkit for pixel classification, object classification, segmentation, and tracking without heavy custom coding.
toolkits.notes: Very practical for mixed plankton images when you need faster iteration than training a bespoke deep model.

toolkits.name: scikit-image
toolkits.install: pip install scikit-image
toolkits.summary: Widely used Python image-processing library for filtering, segmentation, morphology, registration, and measurement.
toolkits.notes: Good backbone when custom plankton, biofilm, or fluorescence workflows need to stay in Python.

toolkits.name: EcoTaxa Python Client
toolkits.install: pip install git+https://github.com/ecotaxa/ecotaxa_py_client.git
toolkits.summary: Python client for the EcoTaxa platform, useful for plankton-image projects, object metadata, and classification-oriented workflows.
good_for: linking microscope outputs to taxonomic projects
toolkits.notes: Most relevant when microscope imaging is part of a plankton-focused labeling and classification workflow.

toolkits.name: PlanktoScope
toolkits.install: Follow the upstream hardware, imaging, and software setup documentation for the full platform.
toolkits.summary: Open imaging platform for plankton observation and quantitative image acquisition, with a strong fit for community monitoring workflows.
toolkits.notes: Useful when you want repeatable plankton imaging hardware instead of only offline image processing.

toolkits.name: QIIME 2 / Rachis Framework
toolkits.install: Use the upstream environment or distribution guidance from qiime2.org for amplicon and microbiome workflows.
toolkits.summary: Widely used framework for marker-gene, microbiome, and amplicon-sequencing analysis with provenance-aware artifacts and plugins.
toolkits.notes: Relevant for day-scale PCR or sequencing follow-up on bacterial or microbial-community dynamics.

toolkits.name: DADA2
toolkits.install: Install from the upstream R package workflow inside a suitable R environment.
toolkits.summary: Widely used amplicon-denoising workflow for high-resolution sequence inference from marker-gene data.
toolkits.notes: Best added when the microcosm workflow moves from microscopy and sensors into marker-gene sequencing.

toolkits.name: APSIM Next Generation
toolkits.install: Follow the official APSIM Next Generation release and installation guidance from the upstream project; it is typically installed as a desktop or managed runtime application.
toolkits.summary: Widely used agricultural systems modeling framework for crop, soil, rotation, and management scenario analysis.
toolkits.notes: Strong choice when the question goes beyond a single crop season into system-level management and agro-ecosystem comparisons.

toolkits.name: PCSE / WOFOST
toolkits.install: Install from pip or from source following the upstream PCSE documentation.
toolkits.summary: Python Crop Simulation Environment with WOFOST-style crop modeling for phenology, biomass, and yield workflows.
toolkits.notes: Very practical when you want a Python-first crop simulator that fits notebook-based workflows.

toolkits.name: AquaCrop-OSPy
toolkits.install: pip install aquacrop
toolkits.summary: Python implementation of AquaCrop-OS with a strong focus on water-limited crop growth, irrigation, and water productivity.
toolkits.notes: Best fit when water balance, irrigation scheduling, or drought stress is central.

toolkits.name: BioCro
toolkits.install: Follow the upstream installation guidance for the BioCro R package and companion C++ codebase.
toolkits.summary: Mechanistic crop-ecophysiology framework for canopy photosynthesis, growth, and biomass simulation in field-crop systems.
toolkits.notes: Best added when the question is more mechanistic than standard yield-focused crop models and needs explicit physiology.

toolkits.name: pyfao56
toolkits.install: pip install pyfao56
toolkits.summary: Python implementation of FAO-56 soil-water balance methods for crop evapotranspiration, irrigation scheduling, and deficit analysis.
toolkits.notes: A strong lightweight option when irrigation and water accounting matter more than full crop-system detail.

toolkits.name: CPlantBox
toolkits.install: Use the upstream installation scripts such as installCPlantBox.py or follow the official setup guidance for Ubuntu and Python environments.
toolkits.summary: Functional-structural plant modeling framework for 3D root-shoot architecture and plant-soil interaction studies.
toolkits.notes: One of the strongest open frameworks for explicit root and plant-soil interaction modeling.

toolkits.name: OpenAlea L-Py
toolkits.install: Install through the upstream OpenAlea or conda-based distribution guidance for L-Py.
toolkits.summary: L-system-based plant modeling environment for branching, organogenesis, architectural development, and visualization.
toolkits.notes: Useful when structural or generative plant form is the core modeling target.

toolkits.name: pyrealm
toolkits.install: pip install pyrealm
toolkits.summary: Ecophysiology and ecosystem-modeling package with productivity and environmental-response modules that fit plant growth and carbon-water studies.
toolkits.notes: A strong bridge between plant growth, carbon cycling, and environmental forcing.

toolkits.name: r3PG
toolkits.install: Install from CRAN or GitHub following the upstream R package guidance for 3-PG workflows.
toolkits.summary: R implementation of the 3-PG forest growth model for plantation productivity, stand development, and management scenario analysis.
toolkits.notes: A practical first choice for woody-plant and plantation questions when a lighter forest-growth model is enough.

toolkits.name: medfate
toolkits.install: Install from the upstream R package source and data workflow described by the medfate project.
toolkits.summary: Forest and shrubland simulation package with explicit water balance, plant hydraulics, and drought-response workflows.
toolkits.notes: Especially useful for woody vegetation where hydraulic stress, transpiration, and stand water balance are central.

toolkits.name: COBRApy
toolkits.install: pip install cobra
toolkits.summary: Core Python framework for constraint-based metabolic modeling, metabolic-growth simulation, flux balance analysis, and dynamic metabolic workflows.
toolkits.notes: Best foundational choice for microbial or metabolism-aware growth models.

toolkits.name: MICOM
toolkits.install: pip install micom
toolkits.summary: Python framework for metabolic modeling of microbial communities with abundance-aware growth and cross-feeding analysis.
toolkits.notes: A strong fit when the question is about microbial consortia rather than single isolates.

toolkits.name: COMETS
toolkits.install: Use the upstream COMETS release or source distribution together with compatible metabolic-model workflows.
toolkits.summary: Community metabolism simulator for microbial consortia with spatial diffusion, metabolite exchange, and dynamic environmental coupling.
toolkits.notes: A strong next step when MICOM is not spatial enough and community metabolism must interact with space or diffusion.

toolkits.name: BacArena
toolkits.install: Install the upstream R package and required metabolic-model dependencies inside a suitable R environment.
toolkits.summary: Agent-based microbial metabolism framework that combines individual microbes, environment grids, and metabolic exchange.
toolkits.notes: Useful when microbial individuals and metabolic exchange both need to stay explicit.

toolkits.name: Community Simulator
toolkits.install: Install from the upstream Python package or source repository.
toolkits.summary: Python framework for consumer-resource and community-assembly simulations in microbial ecology.
toolkits.notes: A good fit when the question is ecological community assembly rather than genome-scale metabolism.

toolkits.name: Tellurium
toolkits.install: pip install tellurium
toolkits.summary: Python environment for SBML-based and kinetic simulation workflows with a strong fit for mechanistic growth and reactor models.
toolkits.notes: Very useful when the model is expressed as reaction kinetics or differential equations.

toolkits.name: COPASI
toolkits.install: Use the official COPASI desktop or command-line distribution from the upstream project.
toolkits.summary: Established simulation platform for biochemical networks, kinetics, parameter estimation, and dynamic systems analysis.
toolkits.notes: A good choice when users need a mature GUI or CLI platform for mechanistic dynamic models.

toolkits.name: PySCeS
toolkits.install: pip install pysces
toolkits.summary: Python simulator for cellular systems and kinetic models that fits mechanistic growth, pathway, and reactor-style analyses.
toolkits.notes: Helpful when you want a lighter Python-native alternative to larger systems-biology platforms.

toolkits.name: NUFEB
toolkits.install: Build from the upstream source and LAMMPS-compatible stack following the official NUFEB guidance.
toolkits.summary: Individual-based simulator for microbial communities, biofilms, and particulate systems in three-dimensional spatial domains.
toolkits.notes: A high-value option when biofilm structure, particle interactions, and spatial gradients matter.

toolkits.name: Vivarium Core
toolkits.install: pip install vivarium-core
toolkits.summary: Composable simulation engine for multi-process biological models that fits custom microbial physiology and community workflows.
toolkits.notes: Best when the team wants to build a custom simulation by wiring multiple process modules together.

toolkits.name: MDSINE2
toolkits.install: Clone the upstream repository and install it with pip following the project instructions.
toolkits.summary: Framework for modeling and inferring microbial dynamics from longitudinal time-series data with interaction structure.
toolkits.notes: Most relevant when repeated measurements drive the microbial-growth question.

toolkits.name: miaSim
toolkits.install: Install the upstream R package and companion microbiome-analysis dependencies in an R environment.
toolkits.summary: Simulation toolkit for microbiome count data and longitudinal perturbation designs, useful for benchmarking microbial ecology analyses.
toolkits.notes: Helpful when the goal is benchmarking methods or generating controlled microbial-community scenarios rather than mechanistic prediction alone.

toolkits.name: pyPESTO
toolkits.install: Install from pip or follow the upstream environment guidance for full optimization backends.
toolkits.summary: Parameter-estimation toolbox for Python with optimization, profile likelihoods, sensitivity, and uncertainty workflows.
toolkits.notes: Best added when a growth model needs careful calibration rather than one-off scenario runs.

toolkits.name: NetLogo
toolkits.install: Download the official NetLogo desktop or headless distribution from the upstream project and use BehaviorSpace or headless runs for scenario sweeps.
toolkits.summary: Widely used agent-based modeling environment for individual- and rule-based ecological simulations, education, and rapid prototyping.
toolkits.notes: A strong first choice when the ecological process is easiest to express as explicit agents and local rules.

toolkits.name: Mesa
toolkits.install: pip install mesa
toolkits.summary: Python-native agent-based modeling framework that fits ecological prototypes, custom rules, and notebook-friendly experiments.
toolkits.notes: Best fit when the modeling workflow should stay close to Python data pipelines and scientific notebooks.

toolkits.name: GAMA Platform
toolkits.install: Use the official desktop or headless GAMA release from the upstream project.
toolkits.summary: Spatially explicit multi-agent simulation platform with strong GIS integration for complex ecology, land-use, and social-ecological system models.
toolkits.notes: Most useful when spatial GIS layers and multiple interacting agent types are central.

toolkits.name: DSSAT Cropping System Model
toolkits.install: Build from the open-source repository or use the official DSSAT distribution and example data from dssat.net.
toolkits.summary: Long-running crop-system modeling framework for crop growth, management, soil, weather, and scenario analysis across agricultural systems.
toolkits.notes: One of the core traditional agricultural process-model systems and a strong complement to APSIM and WOFOST-style workflows.

toolkits.name: SWAT+
toolkits.install: Use the official SWAT+ executables, editor, and setup workflow from the upstream project documentation.
toolkits.summary: Watershed-scale model for hydrology, nutrients, land management, and water-quality scenario analysis.
toolkits.notes: Best fit when basin-scale hydrology and agricultural or watershed management are both important.

toolkits.name: Ecopath with Ecosim
toolkits.install: Download the official EwE desktop software and example models from the Ecopath project site.
toolkits.summary: Established ecosystem and fisheries modeling suite for trophic-balance analysis, biomass flow, and food-web scenario simulation.
toolkits.notes: A very strong default when the research question is explicitly trophic or fisheries-focused.

toolkits.name: LPJ-GUESS
toolkits.install: Build from the official source distribution and follow the project guidance for climate-forcing and run configuration.
toolkits.summary: Dynamic global vegetation model for terrestrial carbon, water, nitrogen, vegetation, and climate-response studies.
toolkits.notes: A strong traditional process model for large-scale terrestrial ecosystem and vegetation-change questions.

toolkits.name: ED2
toolkits.install: Compile the model from source and configure run directories and forcing inputs according to the upstream ED2 instructions.
toolkits.summary: Ecosystem Demography model for vegetation structure, demography, carbon, water, and long-term ecosystem dynamics.
toolkits.notes: Useful when demographic structure and stand composition are central rather than only bulk ecosystem fluxes.

toolkits.name: Biome-BGC
toolkits.install: Use the official Biome-BGC distribution and setup guidance from the project site.
toolkits.summary: Biogeochemical and ecophysiological model for carbon, water, nitrogen, LAI, GPP, and NPP in terrestrial ecosystems.
toolkits.notes: A classic process model when carbon-water-nitrogen cycles and LAI-sensitive ecosystem behavior are the focus.

toolkits.name: CENTURY / DayCent
toolkits.install: Use the official Colorado State University distribution and model documentation for Century or DayCent workflows.
toolkits.summary: General plant-soil nutrient cycling model family for carbon and nutrient dynamics across grasslands, croplands, forests, and savannas.
toolkits.notes: A classic choice for terrestrial carbon and nutrient-cycle questions, especially when soil processes are central.

toolkits.name: RHESSys
toolkits.install: Build from source and follow the RHESSys setup workflow for basin, hillslope, and forcing inputs.
toolkits.summary: Regional Hydro-Ecologic Simulation System for ecohydrology, watershed process coupling, and land-use or climate-change analysis.
toolkits.notes: Most useful when hydrology and ecosystem response need to stay coupled across landscape units.

toolkits.name: LANDIS-II
toolkits.install: Use the official LANDIS-II core model and extension setup guidance from the project site.
toolkits.summary: Forest landscape model for succession, disturbance, management, and extension-based scenario analysis over long time horizons.
toolkits.notes: A strong fit when the question is about forest disturbance, management, and long-term landscape structure.

toolkits.name: Madingley Model
toolkits.install: Use the official Madingley distribution and examples from the project site or associated source repositories.
toolkits.summary: General ecosystem model for multi-trophic ecosystem structure, biodiversity patterns, and human-impact scenario analysis.
toolkits.notes: Best used when the goal is a general ecosystem picture rather than a single taxon or single process.

toolkits.name: RangeShifter 2.0
toolkits.install: Follow the official RangeShifter 2.0 installation and tutorial guidance from the project site.
toolkits.summary: Spatial eco-evolutionary simulation platform for dispersal, range dynamics, connectivity, and species response to landscape change.
toolkits.notes: A strong option when the research focus is dispersal, range change, or landscape connectivity through time.
